review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The reporting inspected recordings and derivatives from sensitive sessions. Organisers described absent permission and expectations that meetings would not be recorded. conclusion_change.previous: The evidence supports separate access, capture and secondary-publication mechanisms across several reported sessions. Zoom’s account attributes entry to publicly shared links and recording to external tools rather than a Zoom breach. WebinarTV’s CEO stated a public-webinar view and host contact policy, while the cases reported posting before contact and participant expectations of restricted access. Removal of the teacher’s session demonstrates one corrective action, but the record does not establish global removal or verified deletion of derivatives. Technical reachability, participant capture and later public derivative use remain separate failures grounded in inspected sessions and attributed organizer testimony. Removal of one session is bounded recovery; the company’s corpus number is not an unauthorized-session count. Bias-correction permissions, model-development security and model-agent admission concern different objects from the supported operational capture/publication mechanism.
